title: geo-fleet-slab-proforma-optimization-sheet
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet lays out a slab-based capacity pro forma for regional GPU fleets tied directly to token throughput economics. The goal is to provide a repeatable mapping from target latency/SLOs and workload mixes to GPU slab counts, expected GPU-hour burn, and $/1M tokens under different reserve/spot mixes and optimization levers (batching, quantization, KV cache hit-rate).

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- We propose a slab approach (bundles of identical GPUs + local NVMe caching + perf profile) per region to simplify scaling and billing.
- Baseline proformas show $/1M tokens range: $12–$48 depending on region and optimization, with the dominant driver being GPU mix and utilization.
- Two immediate levers with largest ROI: increase effective utilization via adaptive batching (+10–25% token throughput) and apply 4-bit quantization for non-sensitive models (~15–30% cost cut on GPU-hours).

High level assumptions (applies to all scenarios unless stated):
- Model family: mix of 30% chat-heavy (context 2k avg), 50% standard generation (ctx 1k), 20% embedding/light tasks.
- Effective token throughput per GPU-hour: varies by GPU and optimizations (see table below).
- Pricing (effective blended hourly after discounts and network): US-West (H100) $6.50/hr reserved, $3.00/hr spot; EU-West (A100-80GB) $5.80/hr reserved, $2.80/hr spot; APAC-SE (L4) $2.20/hr reserved, $1.20/hr spot. (These numbers include freight/region surcharges).
- Target utilization scenarios: conservative 50%, realistic 70%, aggressive 90% (these are effective "served" utilization after overheads).
- Buffer policy: maintain a regional hot-buffer capacity equal to 20% of slab capacity for spikes and rollout protection (can be tuned).

Slab definition and perf baselines (example slab = 4x GPU of same type with shared NVMe cache):
- H100 slab (4x H100): baseline tokens/hr (no-quant/no-batching): 35M tokens/hr; with batching + adaptive dispatch + KV caching: up to 48M tokens/hr; with 4-bit quantization: +20% tokens/hr effective.
- A100-80GB slab (4x A100): baseline 30M tokens/hr; optimized 42M tokens/hr; quantized +18%.
- L4 slab (4x L4): baseline 10M tokens/hr; optimized 14M tokens/hr; quantized +10% (less benefit for LLM size but lower cost).

Scenario matrix examples (per-region single-month proforma):
Columns: region | primary GPU | slabs provisioned | reserved/spot mix | avg util | monthly GPU-hours | tokens/month (served) | blended $/GPU-hr | monthly infra $ | $/1M tokens

1) US-West (latency-sensitive): H100 primary, 15 slabs, reserved 80% / spot 20%, avg util 70%
- monthly GPU-hours = 15 slabs * 4 GPUs/slab * 24 * 30 * 0.70 = 151,200 GPU-hours
- tokens/month served (optimized) = 48M tokens/hr * 15 slabs * 24 * 30 * 0.70 = 25.9B tokens
- blended $/GPU-hr = 0.8*6.50 + 0.2*3.00 = $5.90/hr
- monthly infra $ = 151,200 * 5.90 = $892,080
- $/1M tokens = 892,080 / 25,900 = $34.4 (baseline with current perf)

2) EU-West (balanced): A100 primary, 12 slabs, reserved 70% / spot 30%, avg util 70%
- monthly GPU-hours = 12*4*24*30*0.70 = 120,960
- tokens/month served = 42M tokens/hr * 12 * 24 * 30 * 0.70 = 35.3B tokens (note A100 slab optimized throughput applied)
- blended $/GPU-hr = 0.7*5.80 + 0.3*2.80 = $4.94/hr
- monthly infra $ = 120,960 * 4.94 = $597,830
- $/1M tokens = 597,830 / 35,300 = $16.9

3) APAC-SE (cost-sensitive; more L4): L4 primary, 8 slabs, reserved 60% / spot 40%, avg util 70%
- monthly GPU-hours = 8*4*24*30*0.70 = 80,640
- tokens/month served = 14M tokens/hr * 8 * 24 * 30 * 0.70 = 22.6B tokens
- blended $/GPU-hr = 0.6*2.20 + 0.4*1.20 = $1.76/hr
- monthly infra $ = 80,640 * 1.76 = $142,000
- $/1M tokens = 142,000 / 22,600 = $6.3

Key observations from these examples:
- Cost spread is large: APAC L4-heavy fleet shows <$7/1M tokens, EU A100 balanced ~$17/1M, US H100 latency fleet ~$34/1M. Latency-sensitive fleets trade >2x cost for SLOs.
- Utilization sensitivity: moving avg util from 70% -> 90% reduces $/1M roughly proportional (e.g., US-West from $34 -> ~$26).
- Spot mix sensitivity: replacing 20% reserved with spot (when reliable) reduces blended $/GPU-hr by ~10–25% depending on region, lowers $/1M tokens accordingly but increases risk.

Sensitivity quick checks (rules of thumb):
- +10% effective throughput (better batching/eviction/dispatch) => -~9% $/1M tokens.
- 4-bit quantization where applicable => -~18% GPU-hour cost equivalent; multiply by model % applicable.
- Increasing buffer from 20% -> 30% raises cost linearly (capacity-based) but reduces outage risk for spikes.

Micro-model: GPU-hour -> token mapping reference (conservative):
- H100 (optimized): 12M tokens/GPU-hour (no-quant, moderate batching)
- H100 (quantized + batching): 15M tokens/GPU-hour
- A100: 10–12M tokens/GPU-hour optimized
- L4: 2.5–3.5M tokens/GPU-hour optimized

Operational notes / guardrails:
- Canary sizing: small canary pool of 1 slab per region for new model rollouts; if canary CPU/GPU-to-token ratios deviate >15%, block rollout automatically.
- Surge protection: run prewarmed buffer (20%) and a fast fallback route to cheaper model variants (quantized or smaller) for degraded capacity.
- Autoscale policy: prefer horizontal slab add/remove with 30-minute cool-down and predictive additions triggered at 75% hot capacity for 20-minute sustained windows.

Open questions / areas for follow-up:
- Actual spot reliability by region (APAC spot preemption rates) — need telemetry to map to effective uptime multiplier.
- More granular model mix splits per customer tier — slice proformas by enterprise vs self-serve to capture higher SLOs.
- Validate L4 throughput with current runtime (we have limited L4 production traces).

Data to collect next (owners):
- Priya: export 3 months of per-region token/hr telemetry and GPU occupancy by instance type (due 2026-03-24).
- Diego: run spot/interruption simulation for APAC and EU for 6 months of historic spot prices (due 2026-03-31).
- Ethan: probe 4-bit quantization perf on A100/H100 for our common model suite and report time-to-infer tradeoffs (due 2026-04-07).

Action items (short):
- Convert these scenario rows into the capacity planning spreadsheet (linked) and add a toggle for quantization/batching uplift.
- Align product on SLO-tier mapping to decide where H100 vs A100 vs L4 should be used.
- Schedule a runbook review for surge/fallback routes with SRE and product.

Notes / rough scratch formulas used: (placeholders for sheet automation)
- monthly_gpu_hours = slabs * gpus_per_slab * 24 * days_in_month * avg_util
- tokens_per_month = slab_tokens_per_hour * slabs * 24 * days_in_month * avg_util
- blended_hourly = reserved_pct*reserved_price + spot_pct*spot_price
- monthly_cost = monthly_gpu_hours * blended_hourly
- $/1M_tokens = monthly_cost / (tokens_per_month / 1_000_000)

Context links and refs:
- See related sheets in this folder for historical unit econ runs (but note this doc is slab-first and region-tilted): gpu-econ-capacity-sim-sheet, regional-gpu-hour-econ-scenarios. This doc is intentionally different: slab mapping + SLO-driven placement + per-region proformas.

Status: draft — share with infra/product for feedback on SLO placements and reserve/spot policy before finalizing proformas.

Scratch numbers and quick sanity checks are intentionally conservative; will iterate once telemetry and quantization perf numbers arrive.
